provenance.notes: Our contribution: the irregular 4x10 base template A (every check weight 7, qubit degrees 2 and 3, design rate 1/5) on which the pair-partition rule is applied; the template census that selected it (one side's templates enumerated exhaustively for 3 or 4 block rows, row weight <= 7, column degrees 2..3, up to row and column permutation; X/Z pairs with even row overlaps placed by SAT and ranked by a permanent-vector upper bound, our generalisation of App. A of arXiv:2609.30069 to sparse templates); the choice of pairing for each X-row/Z-row overlap; the lift P = 99 and this exponent draw; the distance screening described in notes/990-198-17.md, and the exact-distance computation (the GF(2) check of each automorphism generator and the set-cover bound, added to cpm_distance's branch-and-bound; the restriction to one root per automorphism orbit is the orbit anchoring of Rowshan and Devitt, arXiv:2609.39395). Construction framework, not ours: the pair-partition construction and its paired-difference equations on CPM exponents are Okada and Kasai's (arXiv:2607.14091), where they are applied to complete J x L templates; the design-rate count R = 1 - J_tot/L_stab and the permanent-vector bound are from Lee, Okada, Maskara, Kasai and Zhou (arXiv:2609.30069), whose outlook names quantum-compatible irregular templates as a natural direction; this entry is one instance in that direction. Quasi-cyclic CSS LDPC codes from circulant permutation matrices go back to Hagiwara and Imai (arXiv:quant-ph/0701020), and CSS pairs of two irregular LDPC codes were analysed by Hagiwara and Imai (arXiv:0801.1361). Board precedents of the same commutation mechanism at weight 8: the (3,8) pair-partition entries codes/904-230-22.json, codes/712-182-20.json and codes/632-162-18.json by @vprusso, codes/824-210-20.json by @MathysRennela, codes/808-206-20.json by @pandey-tushar, codes/568-146-18.json by @nihoniumqc, our codes/928-238-22.json and codes/976-250-22.json, and the published codes/584-150-18.json (Okada-Kasai); @vprusso's entries also cite the lifted-product construction of Panteleev and Kalachev (arXiv:2111.03654); the pairing anneal we used was calibrated on the complete (3,8) template of those entries. The weight-7 entries on the board with the highest kd^2/n are codes/682-20-38.json and codes/762-28-32.json by @FarLab (two-block group-algebra codes, arXiv:2306.16400). In our check (2026-10-22: arXiv:2607.14091, arXiv:2609.30069, the Okada-Kasai project page, web searches) we did not find a pair-partition code on an irregular template or with check weight below 8; literature novelty is not claimed. Distance: confidence exact on both sides; the board shows d <= 17; this code is outside verify/certify.py's current envelope (CONTRIBUTING.md), so the exact value is our evidence, not a certificate. Upper side: Stern information-set decoding found weight-17 logicals on both sides and nothing lighter in 3 seeds x 300 s per side, and the board's verify/heuristic_distance.py (RIS, orbit pass over 5 symmetry partitions, 400000 gf2_fast trials) returned 'corroborated', d 17 on both sides. Lower side: an exhaustive branch-and-bound search (our gexact, built on the branch-and-bound of Okada and Kasai's cpm_distance, github.com/kasaikenta/pair-partition-cpm-css-codes, with one root per orbit of the GF(2)-verified Z_99 shift, the orbit anchoring of Rowshan and Devitt, arXiv:2609.39395) found no logical of weight <= 16 on either side; cross-checked with no automorphisms and with gexact in cpm_distance's mode (its roots and lower bound); details in notes/990-198-17.md.
